title: TESS transits at Gaia DR3 conjunction times show that most short-period low-mass SB1 orbits are not genuine low-mass companions, and give 51 uncatalogued candidates (6,863 stars, P < 10 d)
abstract: We tested Gaia DR3 single-lined spectroscopic orbits with periods below 10 days, dwarf primaries brighter than G = 13.5, and minimum companion masses below 0.15 Msun. We used TESS-SPOC light curves of 6,863 stars. We searched each light curve for a box dip at the Gaia period and at eight control periods. Then we compared the excess with the number of transits that is expected if every orbit is genuine and the companion has the implied mass. We calibrated the expected number with 2,000 injected transits (93% recovery). The Gaia period gave 393 eclipse-like detections. The control periods gave a mean of 54. The excess (339 +/- 20) is 0.25 +/- 0.01 of the expected number, and 0.11 +/- 0.01 for transit-shaped dips with the expected depth. The ratio increases with Gaia orbit significance, from 0.04 below K/sigma = 10 to 0.7-1.2 above 40. It is 0.009 +/- 0.008 for minimum masses below 0.03 Msun: TESS shows about 3 excess transits where 304 are expected. The dips occur at the Gaia-predicted conjunction phase: 60-73% are within 0.1 cycle, against 19% for control detections (p < 1e-15). Thus most of the TESS signals belong to the Gaia orbits. 121 transit-consistent systems are not in the TOI, Gaia DR3 eclipsing-binary, VSX or TESS EB (sectors 1-26) catalogues. Of these, 51 pass stricter checks (tier 1). Most are probably M-dwarf companions with Gaia masses of 0.08-0.15 Msun. Limitations: we did not do follow-up; blends and other catalogues are not excluded; about 28 false alarms are expected among the transit-consistent detections; the completeness model omits grazing transits and limb darkening; spurious solutions and inclined heavier companions cannot be separated.

display.caption: Phase of the TESS dip relative to the Gaia-predicted primary conjunction. Transit-consistent detections at the Gaia period (blue: catalogued; orange: not catalogued) cluster at phase 0. Detections at control periods (grey) are uniform.
